message: No detected input validation: The only check present is a soft warning in revise_report_df about unexpected column names (print statement), but there are no schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards on the data loaded via pd.read_csv in load_data.py.
No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from local flat files via pd.read_csv with no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks; no remote sources are used.

No detected label flipping detection: The code only calls value_counts() to identify majority/minority classes for upsampling; there is no validation of label values against an expected set, no comparison of label distributions for anomalies, and no label-noise detection tool is used.
No detected data poisoning defenses: The pipeline reads CSV data and splits/upsamples it without any outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious samples before training.

No detected model integrity verification: The code instantiates sklearn models directly from constructors (e.g., GradientBoostingClassifier(), RandomForestClassifier()) and trains them in-process; no pretrained weights or serialized models are loaded, so there is no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision implemented.
No detected label distribution validation: The code handles class imbalance via upsampling but performs no explicit validation of label distribution or expected label set before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no backdoor defense, trigger detection, activation-pattern analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) or mechanisms are used anywhere in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or stress tests are used anywhere in the evaluation pipeline.

No detected input sanitization: The callback_image function uses ast.literal_eval/json.dumps on hoverData but performs no shape, range, or schema validation on the hover payload before using it to construct file paths, making it vulnerable to path traversal or KeyError on malformed input.
No detected output bounds checks: The inference/display path reads pre-computed CSV reports and encodes images without any checks on probability bounds, NaN values, or prediction sanity.

No detected prompt injection defenses: The pipeline uses traditional sklearn classifiers (GradientBoosting, RandomForest, LogisticRegression, GaussianNB), not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
